item.title: Purdue basketball returns to cold shooting form in loss to DePaul
item.description: FORT MYERS, Florida − The 3-point shooting slump Purdue basketball seemingly shot its way out of during a four-game winning streak returned once the Boilermakers left the friendly rims of Mackey Arena. A disastrous shooting showcase highlighted DePaul's 65-56 victory over Purdue (4-3) at the Fort Myers Tip-Off Classic at Suncoast Credit Union Arena. During its four-game winning streak, Purdue shot 40.5% from 3-point range. As was the case in losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season, the Boilermakers couldn't find a way to win when the shots weren't going in. Purdue made 4 of 28 3-pointers (14.3%) and closed the game missing 10 straight shots. The Blue Demons (6-0) capitalized on Purdue's inability to make shots in a game that became evident early would be defined by defense. Purdue basketball turning point vs. DePaul Purdue played right into DePaul's hands, enduring a back alley fight the Blue Demons force opponents into. Once the Boilermakers embraced the physicality, they went on a 15-2 run with a spark from the bench while Daniel Jacobsen watched the final 16:38 of the first half on the bench with two fouls. Getting to halftime with a 33-32 lead without Jacobsen while turning the ball over eight times and shooting 9.1% from 3-point range came on Purdue playing rugged and dominating the rebounding. Purdue scored 11 second chance points in the first half. A 3-pointer by Koree Cotton gave DePaul the lead to start the second half and Purdue's struggles helped the Blue Demons stay in front. Purdue did come back to tie the game at 54 with 5:30 to go, but Jack Benter missed the second of two free throw attempts with a chance to give Purdue the lead. The Boilermakers missed 10 straight shots after that and watched a close game become a gap too big to recover from. Game MVP Layden Blocker's ability to get by Purdue defenders and convert at the rim was problematic for the Boilermakers all night. Blocker scored 16 points to go with 3 steals and 2 assists. 3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. DePaul Luke Ertel: The freshman is built for big moments and fresh off a game where he made 8 3-pointers in a win over Oakland , Ertel was lifting the Boilermakers through adversity with another big night. Foul trouble derailed it. Ertel scored a team-high 12 points. Raleigh Burgess: Without Jacobsen, Burgess played stellar defense off the bench in the first half. He had 4 points, 3 rebounds and an assist in nine minutes, helping the Boilermakers survive without their 7-foot-4 center. Gicarri Harris: The junior guard does so many little things that don't show up on a stat sheet. On top of that, he's also filling the box score. Harris finished with 11 points, 6 rebounds and a steal. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. This article originally appeared on Lafayette Journal & Courier: Purdue basketball returns to cold shooting form in loss to DePaul

item.title: Singleton scores 22 as Iowa State opens Players Era Tournament with W
item.description: Tre Singleton (0) of the Iowa State Cyclones looks on before a game against the San Diego State Aztecs during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena on Nov. 24, 2026 in Las Vegas. | Zach Del Bello/Players Era LAS VEGAS – Tre Singleton scored a game-high 22 points and Dom Pleta hauled in a game-high 10 rebounds as Iowa State powered past San Diego State 81-68 Tuesday night. San Diego State held an early 8-7 lead at the first media timeout. Iowa State responded as Prather knocked down a 3-pointer to put the Cyclones ahead 13-10, followed immediately by a Singleton layup. That sequence capped a 12-2 run over 3:36, pushing Iowa State’s lead to 17-10. The Aztecs answered after Singleton was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Luka Skorić sank a pair of free throws and Isaiah Sy hit a 3-pointer to trim the deficit to 17-15. Buchanan halted the momentum with a dunk to push the cushion back to four. Moments later, Prather sank three consecutive free throws and Singleton drilled a 3-pointer to extend the lead to double digits at 25-15. Iowa State later reeled off a 7-0 run over 95 seconds, building a 37-25 advantage with 3:16 left in the first half behind 11 early points from Singleton. Sy added a late layup for San Diego State, and after Pleta’s half-court heave missed at the horn, Iowa State carried a 41-34 lead into halftime. Singleton led all scorers with 14 points at the break. San Diego State trimmed the margin to two points early in the second half. A Taj Manning layup restored a 50-44 cushion, though Manning soon picked up his fourth foul. The Aztecs failed to capitalize, going 0-for-2 at the foul line following a lane violation, keeping Iowa State ahead 56-50 with 11 minutes remaining. The Cyclones seized full control from there. A Prather 3-pointer and two free throws from Singleton stretched the lead back to 11. Iowa State then mounted its fourth 7-0-or-better run of the night, scoring seven points in just 64 seconds to build a 71-57 cushion at the 5:18 mark. San Diego State center Bear Cherry fouled out with the Cyclones leading by 15 with 85 seconds remaining. Prather finished with 16 points. With the win, Iowa State advances to take on No. 9 Tennessee on Thursday.

item.title: MOTM Poll: Spoils Shared in the Emirates as Dortmund Tie Arsenal
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 24: Christos Tzolis of Arsenal and Joane Gadou of Borussia Dortmund challenge for the ball during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Arsenal FC and Borussia Dortmund at Arsenal Stadium on November 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images) | Getty Images Dortmund walk away from their hardest UCL fixture of the league phase, Arsenal away from home, and left with their heads held high. Despite falling behind within 10 minutes, Niko Kovac’s men bounced back in the second half and leave London with a point. Like we saw against Bayern, Dortmund were on the back-foot but still looked dangerous and up for the challenge. It was a great performance and I recommend checking out Adam’s Post Match Reactions here ! Here are my MOTM nominees: Maximilian Beier Maxi Beier’s lone goal came from the 24-year-old’s lone shot in this match, but it was well taken. Almost as important was Beier’s verticality. When Dortmund won the ball in their own third, Beier made excellent runs and consistently had Gabriel’s number. Not many players have managed that in a UCL game! Joane Gadou I was watching this game with some friends, and in the 60th minute of the match, one said, “Joane Gadou isn’t going to be in Dortmund for long.” The 19-year-old Frenchman displayed every facet of his game in this match. He led Borussia Dortmund in defensive contributions and won 80% of his duels. Gadou’s two biggest attributes are his physicality, allowing him to recover in a way very few players on the planet can when Dortmund loses possession, and his ability to read the game, allowing him to push forward. Obviously I’m burying the lede here: Gadou’s 60-yard sprint up the field to assist Maxi Beier on the goal. I wouldn’t be surprised if the world’s biggest teams have already called Ole Book about Gadou’s availability. Daniel Svensson Last time I nominated Daniel Svensson, I was (rightly) crucified. This time, I stand by it! The left wing-back led Borussia Dortmund in chances created and created three “big chances,” according to FotMob . His cutbacks into the box were dangerous, and he was constantly an outlet for Dortmund’s defense. I will admit that on the other side of the ball, Svensson wasn’t perfect. Madueke found space behind Svensson when the Swede pushed forward, and Schlotterbeck was often forced to cover. This is partially on Svensson for not being able to cover ground the same way a player like Gadou can, but it’s also simply a byproduct of how Kovac wants Dortmund’s wing-backs to play. Joey Veerman In the past, I’ve written about Joey Veerman’s struggles against teams that press in midfield or try to dictate possession. Today, however, Veerman shone against a Mikel Arteta team whose whole identity is dictating possession. Veerman excelled as a two-way midfielder with 90% pass accuracy, 10 passes into the final third, and 11 defensive contributions. It was a great shift from Ve

item.title: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
item.description: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

item.title: Michigan Basketball gets embarrassed by Creighton in Players Era
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 24: Trey McKenney #1 of the Michigan Wolverines drives past Katrelle Harmon #5 of the Creighton Bluejays during the second half during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at T-Mobile Arena on November 24, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Players Era/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Michigan Wolverines were dominated in a 99-73 loss to the Creighton Blue Jays in the first round of the Players Era tournament in Las Vegas on Tuesday. Michigan is searching for answers, falling to 3-3 following a second straight loss. Here’s how it all went down. Final pic.twitter.com/uqrZ4awz1S — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 25, 2026 FIRST HALF Both teams traded punches in the early minutes as Michigan took an 8-6 lead following a fastbreak layup from guard Roddy Gayle Jr, followed by 3-pointers from guards Trey McKenney and Ricky Liburd to extend the early lead to 17-14. However, Creighton completely seized momentum in the ensuing minutes, putting together a game-changing 20-2 run to build a 38-24 lead. The Blue Jays were led by guard Wes Enis, who knocked down back to back triples to fuel the run. @wesenis21 LETTING IT FLY ‼️ #GoJays | #CreightonMBB pic.twitter.com/yobvu5kXNY — Creighton Men’s Basketball (@BluejayMBB) November 24, 2026 Michigan tried to fight back as guard Elliot Cadeau scored an and-1 to stop the run and cut the deficit to 38-27, but the Blue Jays were just too hot from beyond the arc. Creighton finished the half on a 16-6 run to take a 59-38 lead at halftime. The Wolverines committed an alarming 13 turnovers in the first half alone and shot a putrid 34.3 percent from the field. According to ESPN, trailing by 21 points was Michigan’s largest halftime deficit against an unranked opponent since 2005. HALFTIME: Michigan 38, Creighton 59 SECOND HALF Michigan’s frontcourt got going offensively to open the second half, as center Moustapha Thiam and forward JP Estrella knocked down a pair of 3-pointers. But the defense couldn’t get enough stops to make a dent in the double digit deficit. Estrella continued his solid start to the second half by scoring an and-1 layup and sinking a hook shot, but Michigan still trailed 73-58 with 13:50 remaining. Creighton turned it up a notch again, going on a 17-4 run to extend the lead to 90-62. From deep! 👌 3️⃣ #GoJays | #CreightonMBB pic.twitter.com/D3TxNarjZF — Creighton Men’s Basketball (@BluejayMBB) November 25, 2026 The Blue Jays eventually cruised to a runaway 99-73 win as Michigan suffered an embarrassing loss on a national stage. Michigan committed a season-worst 17 turnovers, while allowing 27 points off turnovers and 29 bench points in the loss. FINAL SCORE: Michigan 73, Creighton 99 MICHIGAN STAT LEADERS F JP Estrella: 22 points, 9 rebounds C Moustapha Thiam: 12 points, 8 rebounds G Trey McKenney: 10 points, 3 assists G Elliot Cadeau: 10 points G Roddy Gayle Jr: 8 points, 10 rebounds, 6 assists CREIGHTON ST

item.title: Curt Cignetti will have nobody to blame but himself if Indiana misses out on College Football Playoff
item.description: Since Curt Cignetti became Indiana’s head coach, the Hoosiers have won 36 out of 40 games, been to the College Football Playoff twice, won a Big Ten title and hung a national championship banner in Memorial Stadium. Even now, long past the point of Indiana football’s new reality becoming normal, it’s a staggering achievement with almost no comparison in the history of sports. But even the best of the best have a blind spot. With Cignetti, it’s the schedule. It’s always the schedule. The CFP committee ranked Indiana No. 14 on Tuesday, putting the Hoosiers in a perilous position heading into the final week of the regular season. Though key results around the country will still impact the rankings, and the committee has made some surprising moves at the last minute before, here’s the tough part for Indiana: The only way to significantly improve their résumé is by getting into the Big Ten championship game and winning it, which would get them in the field automatically. Anything short of that will leave Indiana vulnerable. And it’s (mostly) their own fault. Or, to be more specific, it’s Cignetti’s fault for refusing to acknowledge that non-conference games are important. With Cignetti, it’s not that Indiana has a tough time getting a high-profile opponent to play them. It’s not a financial calculation. It’s a sneering, unserious contempt for any suggestion that Indiana has a responsibility as a premier program to play non-conference games that are worth watching. And now it might really cost him. “We figured we would just adopt the SEC’s scheduling philosophy,” Cignetti said at Big Ten media day before the 2025 season. “Some people don't like it. I'm more focused in on those nine conference games.” But what if those nine conference games don’t give you enough opportunities for good wins? Indiana coach Curt Cignetti reacts during the Hoosiers' overtime loss to Washington on Saturday. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Steph Chambers via Getty Images Indiana has had, by all measures, another outstanding season at 9-2. The Hoosiers lost at home to Ohio State because receiver Nick Marsh was barely out of bounds when he caught the would-be winning touchdown and then again last weekend at Washington because it went 1-for-3 on field goals and lost by three points in overtime. By the same token, Indiana has lived on the margins all season long, winning four one-score games and pulling off a couple unlikely comebacks. They’re probably right about where they should be. It’s not Indiana’s fault the Big Ten has had a strange year, but the selection committee can only judge what they see on tape. Besides a pretty good win over No. 15 Southern Cal, Indiana has nothing else to put in front of the committee and argue that it’s done enough to be in the CFP. Cignetti built a scheduling philosophy around playing nine Big Ten games, thinking that the league would give Indiana enough chances for notable wins. item.title: Kevin Vallejos denies cheating at UFC Qatar, slams Aljamain Sterling – ‘Doesn’t know how to lose’
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 07: Aljamain Sterling enters the Octagon in a featherweight bout during the UFC 310 event at T-Mobile Arena on December 07, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Red-hot Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Featherweight prospect Kevin Vallejos believes Aljamain Sterling is having trouble accepting his UFC Qatar loss. Vallejos scored the biggest victory of his career this past weekend (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026), defeating the former Bantamweight champion via unanimous decision inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Two judges awarded Vallejos all three rounds, while the third scored the Featherweight co-main event 29-28. The fight was much closer than those scorecards suggest, however. Sterling outlanded Vallejos by one significant strike in each of the first two rounds, but “El Chino” connected with the more damaging shots and completely shut down Sterling’s wrestling. The former champion completed just one of his 12 takedown attempts across 15 minutes. Sterling believes he did enough to win, while fellow Featherweight contender Lerone Murphy labeled the decision a “robbery.” Vallejos can understand Sterling thinking he won a close fight, but he remains confident the judges reached the correct decision. “That’s fine that he feels like that,” Vallejos told Yahoo Sports!. “I mean, I feel like I won, but it wasn’t something that was super obvious. It was a super strategic fight.” “How I saw it was I completely neutralized his best weapons, which was his grappling, and even in the striking — it was close, but I won that,” he continued. “I hurt him more than he hurt me. So, I felt like I won the fight.” Sterling’s criticism did not stop with the scorecards. While reviewing the fight, “Funk Master” questioned how Vallejos repeatedly escaped deep takedown attempts, claiming he had never experienced an opponent slipping out of his grasp so easily. Sterling stopped short of directly accusing Vallejos of greasing but certainly floated the possibility. Vallejos did not appreciate the insinuation. “At the end of the day, I have a lot of respect for Aljamain Sterling, and to be honest, I feel like he completely disrespected me and my performance by saying that,” Vallejos said. “At the end of the day, he can feel bad about it or not, but he’s 37 years old, and he clearly doesn’t know how to lose.” “I specifically trained really hard to neutralize his grappling, and I did that,” he continued. “If he wants to make that excuse, that is fine, but that’s not how it was.” Vallejos also responded on social media, inviting Sterling to train in Argentina so he could learn the secrets behind his takedown defense. “We don’t need greasing,” Vallejos wrote. “We simply just get up.” Grease or no grease, the official result is not changing. Vallejos is now 5-0 inside the Octagon and has officially entered the Featherweight title conversation after handing Sterling his second loss at 145 pounds. For complete UFC Qatar results, coverag

item.title: Providence's shooting woes prove costly in Maui loss to No. 8 Arizona
item.description: Caleb Holt scored 21 points and Motiejus Krivas added 20 as No. 8 Arizona cruised to an 84-66 victory over Providence in the Maui Invitational semifinals on Tuesday, Nov. 24, in Lahaina, Hawaii. The Wildcats (6-1) will face Ole Miss, a 73-63 winner over No. 19 BYU, in Wednesday's tournament final. Arizona has won three previous Maui Invitational titles, including in its last appearance in 2022. Holt had his second straight 20-point performance and fourth of the season, making 6 of 9 shots from the field and 3 of 4 from 3-point range. Krivas was 7 of 9 from the field to go with seven rebounds, four blocks and three assists. Arizona has had at least one player score 20 or more points in every game this season. Ivan Kharchenkov contributed 15 points, six rebounds and eight assists as Arizona shot 51.9% overall and 10 of 19 from 3-point range. Providence (5-2), which had defeated VCU, 72-66, on Monday, got 22 points on 8-of-13 shooting from Ryan Mela, but the rest of the team was 17 of 52. The Friars were 7 of 28 from 3-point range. Arizona led 48-26 at halftime but Providence scored the first eight points of the second half. The Wildcats didn't make a field goal for nearly five minutes but then made three in a row to get the lead to 57-38. The Friars were 1 of 11 from 3-point range in the first half but started the second half 4 of 6 from deep. They got as close as 57-44 on an Elijah Saunders 3-pointer, but Arizona made 9 of 13 to go up, 74-52, with 7:51 to go. Holt scored nine consecutive points for Arizona as the Wildcats pushed their lead to 21-10 with 11:23 remaining in the first half. A subsequent 11-0 run, including seven straight by Krivas, extended the margin to 34-13. The Friars, who won the inaugural Maui Invitational in 1984, were set to face BYU in the third-place game on Wednesday afternoon. This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Providence's shooting woes prove costly in Maui loss to No. 8 Arizona

item.title: College Football Playoff rankings show’s inability to start on time adds to ongoing frustrations
item.description: Credit: ESPN Many people will tell you that the weekly College Football Playoff ranking show on ESPN only exists to cause arguments and get people mad. And if so, they do an amazing job. Every week, the new rankings are announced; there are at least one or two inexplicable decisions followed by unsatisfactory explanations , and then everyone in the college football world spends the next two days complaining about them . If that were it, it would be one of the most agonizing viewing experiences of any college football fan’s week. But there’s an extra wrinkle added to the weekly appointment that turns the annoyance and frustration up to 11: The dang show never starts on time . Tuesday’s rankings reveal, the fourth of the 2026 season, was scheduled to start at 7:30 p.m. ET. That didn’t happen because the Creighton-Michigan game beforehand ran long, and ESPN wasn’t going to cut away, even though it was a Bluejay blowout of the Wolverines. The rankings reveal didn’t actually get underway until 8:15 p.m. ET, a whopping 45 minutes later. Adding even more frustration, they’ll have to hustle because ESPN is set to air No. 23 Louisville vs. No. 9 Texas Tech immediately afterward. That game tips off at 8:00 p.m. ET, so not only will they have to rush through the rankings and explanations of whatever dumb thing they did tonight, but fans of that game will either miss the start or have to scramble to find an alternative channel. All of it just puts an annoying cherry on top of what is already an unnecessarily stupid showcase. PSA: The CFP Rankings are supposed to be at 7:30 p.m. They will not be. Because the basketball game preceding it just went to halftime. It’ll likely be after 8. — Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) November 24, 2026 It’d be nice if the CFP rankings show were a show that actually started at a specific scheduled time, and not a show that got squeezed in between basketball games every week. — Nicole Auerbach (@NicoleAuerbach) November 25, 2026 Or maybe a little later. After 47 years, you’d think ESPN would know how long a college basketball game takes and schedule accordingly. Yet here we are. — Andy Staples (@AndyStaples) November 25, 2026 When I am CFB Commissioner you will catch the conclusion of Creighton-Michigan on ESPN+ — Josh Pate (@JoshPateCFB) November 25, 2026 Maybe, as some have suggested, the weekly CFP rankings meeting should just be an email . item.title: Phillies in tough spot after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit
item.description: Phillies in tough spot after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies were among the disappointed parties after Teruaki Sato reportedly agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract with the Chicago Cubs . The agreement, reported on Tuesday, leaves the Phillies searching for a middle-of-the-order bat while also extending their drought in signing Japanese players. According to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Scott Lauber , the Phillies offered a multi-year deal to the 27-year-old Japanese slugger before Sato went with the Cubs' $120 million offer. Details of the reported Phillies offer are unknown. Sato was of interest to the Phillies for several reasons. Playing for the Hanshin Tigers, the slugger led Japan's Central League with a .306 batting average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs. While he is a below-average defender at third base and corner outfield, the Phillies were reportedly ready to play him in left field. After failing to close Sato, the Phillies remain one of the three MLB teams that have yet to sign a player from Nippon Professional Baseball to a major league contract. They were interested in Yoshinobu Yamamoto three years ago, even offering him a deal north of $300 million, but the Japanese ace eventually signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers on a 12-year, $325 million deal. MORE: Why Yankees didn't match Cubs' $120 million offer to Teruaki Sato Phillies' next plan of action after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit After finishing 19th in runs and 22nd in OPS, their lowest marks of the Bryce Harper era (since 2019), Dave Dombrowski & Co. are making efforts to revitalize the Phillies lineup. Their efforts faced a setback on Tuesday after Sato agreed to a deal with the Cubs over the Phillies' multi-year offer. The Phillies' search for a middle-of-the-order right-handed bat to balance out their left-handed-heavy batting lineup could bring them to the doorsteps of Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki. Arozarena recorded his sixth consecutive season with at least 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases in 2026, while also posting a career-best .865 OPS. On the other hand, Suzuki has averaged 24 home runs and an .833 OPS over his last four seasons with the Cubs. The soon-to-be 32-year-olds, who rejected their respective qualifying offers, are seeking a four- or five-year deal this offseason. This may not be the best situation for the Phillies, who will also have to surrender draft-pick compensation and international bonus money to sign either player. In case the Phillies don't want to go in that direction, they may explore a trade with the Dodgers for Teoscar Hernandez. The veteran outfielder will earn $22 million in 2027 and could give the Phillies a right-handed boost to their lineup. item.title: Rome Odunze reveals Jeffery Simmons’ overall impact for Bears
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Rome Odunze reveals Jeffery Simmons’ overall impact for Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Chicago Bears (8-2) prepare for a Thanksgiving Day game against the Detroit Lions (8-2) on Thursday afternoon, the team is looking to excel on both sides of the ball so they can head into next week as the leaders of the NFC North. With Bears defensive star Jeffery Simmons making an early impression for the team after the in-season trade with the Tennessee Titans, wide receiver Rome Odunze would give insight into how Simmons is impacting the team. Playing in three games for Chicago, Simmons already has five sacks to go along with 14 total tackles, but besides bringing individual stellar play, Odunze tells Jordan Schultz on the “Schultz report” that he’s brought a “swagger” to the team. “He just made an instant impact as soon as he got here with the defense,” Odunze said. “Obviously, their leadership, their swagger about him as well; he has that factor as well. But it’s the whole team in general, not just the defense; he impacts the organization as a whole. So just seeing him here and seeing him do his thing on the field, off the field, it is tremendous for us.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) I asked #Bears WR Rome Odunze about the impact Jeffery Simmons is making — on and off the field. I LOVED his answer 👇👇 https://t.co/GCCGoe3F9g pic.twitter.com/IVETgGGf8w — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 24, 2026 Rome Odunze continues on the impact of the Bears’ Jeffery Simmons There’s no denying that it’s impressive when a player on one side of the ball can impact others on the other side, as Odunze says Simmons does. Looking at Odunze, he’s recorded 36 catches for 573 yards with one touchdown pass so far this season, as he continues to show Simmons’ impact within the team and the city of Chicago. “With a player like that, I mean, he’s inspiring folks out there. When he’s playing ball, he’s got his orange sleeves on, you know, showing his daughter that he’s out there making plays,” Odunze said. “So yeah, his impact definitely reaches further in the field for sure, especially for the city of Chicago, which I know has fully embraced him, and is glad that he’s here.” At any rate, it remains to be seen how Simmons continues to help the Bears, with a huge test on Thursday afternoon against the Lions. item.title: Michigan basketball shot down by Creighton in Players Era opener
item.description: LAS VEGAS — The Wolverines will be glad they won’t have to see another Big East team anytime soon. After falling to UConn three weeks ago and to Villanova this past weekend , Creighton put a quick end to Michigan’s Players Era title defense with a 99-73 blowout loss in the opening round at T-Mobile Arena on Tuesday, Nov. 24. J.P. Estrella had 22 points and nine rebounds and Moustapha Thiam had 12 points and eight rebounds for the Wolverines (3-3), which have lost consecutive contests since they lost three straight in March 2025. During last season’s national title campaign, Michigan never lost back-to-back games. The loss dropped Michigan into the consolation bracket, where it will face No. 17 Miami (Fla.) at 3:30 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 26. The Hurricanes lost to TCU, 84-71, in their opener. This one got out of hand in hurry. After a solid start, Michigan fell apart on both ends. Creighton (5-1) shot the lights out from 3-point range. The Wolverines made four shots over the final 12 minutes of the first half. A six-point lead for Michigan turned into a 21-point halftime deficit it couldn’t recover from. Michigan tried to fight back behind its frontcourt duo of Estrella and Thiam. The two bigs each made a 3-pointer during a string of seven unanswered points. Estrella later scored five straight on his own to cut Creighton’s lead to 73-58 with 13:50 to play. But in an outing where Michigan allowed a season-high 16 3-pointers and lost the turnover battle by a 17-6 margin, it couldn’t make a serious push and apply any sort of game pressure. And if that wasn’t enough, a 15-2 burst by Creighton made it 90-62 with 6:49 to go and put it well out of reach. Wes Enis led Creighton’s offensive assault with 30 points and eight 3-pointers. BJ Davis added 21 points. The Bluejays entered the game averaging 10.8 made 3-pointers and 19.6 forced turnovers per game. They made 12 3s in the first half alone – tying the most 3s Michigan has given up in an entire game this season – and scored 27 points off turnovers. Things got off to a rough start before the game even began, with the PA announcer stating Malachi Brown was starting instead of Estrella and that Michigan was coached by Dusty May. Perhaps that was a sign that things weren’t going to go right for the Wolverines. When the game tipped, it looked like an even matchup between two teams that take a bunch of 3-pointers. Creighton scored its first 12 points from beyond the arc, with Enis making three deep balls in the first three-and-a-half minutes. Michigan had success crashing the offensive glass and making four of its first six shots from long range. And it wasn’t just one guy doing the damage from deep. Elliot Cadeau, Trey McKenney, Ricky Liburd and Estrella each knocked down a 3-pointer to give the Wolverines a 22-16 lead with 12:24 left in the first half. But things quickly went sideways for Michigan, as Creighton ripped off a 22-2 run in a six-minute span. The Wolverines were forcing shots during a 1-for-13

item.title: 3 takeaways from Michigan’s demoralizing loss to Creighton
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 24: BJ Davis #24 of the Creighton Bluejays drives to the basket against the Michigan Wolverines during the first half during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at T-Mobile Arena on November 24, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Players Era/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Michigan Wolverines got off to a rough start in the Players Era 16; in front of a sparse crowd in Las Vegas, the Wolverines got destroyed, falling to Creighton, 99-73. Creighton is the fourth Big East team Michigan plays this season: UConn was picked to finish first in the conference preseason poll , Villanova and Marquette were picked to finish third and fourth, respectively, and Creighton was picked to finish second. In the Bluejays’ first season post-Greg McDermott era, Creighton beat a good Iowa team a little over a week ago, but they also lost to a Kansas State team ranked 106th in KenPom. A year ago , Michigan thrived in this event, with three victories by a combined margin of 110 points sparking the national championship run. The basketball team we saw today looked like a far cry from that historically-good squad; Creighton kept making threes and broke down a lethargic Michigan defense. The Wolverines find themselves at 3-3, losing two games in a row for the first time since falling to No. 13 Maryland and No. 8 Michigan State in March of 2025. Michigan’s roster has completely changed since then, but the turnover problems that plagued the first year of the Dusty May era have reared their ugly heads again. The Wolverines turned the ball over a season-high 17 times, as Creighton scored on the other end with relative ease. This was a horrendous start to Feast Week for the Wolverines; it’s time for the more experienced players on this team to step up to make sure this two-game losing skid doesn’t turn into a streak. Here are some takeaways from the loss. Turnover troubles put Michigan in a big hole Creighton’s defense entered this game ranked third in the country in turnover percentage and sixth in steal percentage, so the Wolverines really needed to take care of the ball, especially after turning it over 15 times in the Villanova loss . Turnovers plagued the Wolverines early in this one, with Michigan turning the ball over seven times in the first 11 minutes of the half. Those turnovers helped spark a 22-2 Creighton run that gave the Bluejays an 14-point lead. The turnovers contributed to Michigan’s first half offensive struggles, as the Wolverines had a stretch where they missed 11 of 12 shots. That Creighton lead ballooned up to 20, as Michigan looked completely out of sorts on both ends of the floor. The Wolverines put themselves in a really big hole in that first half, shooting just 34.3 percent from the field while losing the turnover battle, 13-3. item.title: Tom Pelissero names the NFL head coach who just went from almost being fired to turning his team around
item.description: Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images NFL insider Tom Pelissero believes it is too early to make an assessment over how many coaches will be fired in the offseason. Pelissero told The Rich Eisen Show that too many divisions and situations are in flux, with narratives across the league still changing. He pointed to the Washington Commanders, and how head coach Dan Quinn has turned the team’s situation around. Pelissero says Dan Quinn was on the hot seat, but now after their big Monday Night Football win over the Cincinnati Bengals, they are a team with some buzz. He explained: “There’s a lot of teams right now that are hanging on “A month ago, most people would have said Dan Quinn gets fired. Now you’re like, “This team has continued to play, right?” “They are playing hard for him, they are playing way over the level of what they have defensively.” Show host Rich Eisen agreed, noting that the 4-5-1 Commanders are only two wins back from the New York Giants in the NFC East, and also have the tie-breaker over them after their 24-21 win in Week 10. He noted: “The Commanders are the team that can catch the Giants if they’re somehow two games better than them the rest of the way.” Of course, it could all quickly flip back the other way for Washington and Quinn, but right now they are finally back on an upward trajectory. Colts coach beware Pelissero did pick out Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen as one who could have a bleak future. “I don’t think anything’s 100%. I think it’s fair game to say Shane Steichen’s obviously got a lot on the line, and we have to see, and he’s fighting with one hand behind his back based on the personnel that they’ve got.” The Colts are currently tearing everything down after trading away players, firing their GM, and releasing quarterback Daniel Jones. They are currently 3-8 and all but confirmed to miss the playoffs. Following WVU’s 34-31 loss to Houston on November 21, Rodriguez was seen visibly upset with defensive coordinator Zac Alley. The heated interaction quickly became a talking point among Mountaineers fans, especially considering how poorly the defense has performed throughout the season. Now, Rodriguez is acknowledging that he could have handled the situation differently. The admission comes as West Virginia prepares to close its regular season, with questions surrounding the program’s defensive future continuing to grow. WVU’s Rich Rodriguez Addresses Heated Moment With Zac Alley According to Spencer Ripchik , who shared Rodriguez’s comments on X on November 24, the Mountaineers head coach was asked about his relationship with Alley following the public confrontation. Rodriguez insisted everything between the two coaches was “all good,” but he also acknowledged losing his composure. “I probably shouldn’t yell like that. Lose my temper. I should keep more composed. But I can get kind of emotional,” Rodriguez said, according to Ripchik. Those words are significant coming from a coach who has never been afraid to show his emotions on the sideline. Rodriguez’s intensity has followed him throughout his coaching career, but this particular moment attracted attention because it involved one of his own assistants. item.title: US to host 2028 Copa América amid criticism
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the trophy before the start of the CONMEBOL Copa America 2024 final soccer match between Argentina and Colombia at Hard Rock Stadium. (is associated with: «US to host 2028 Copa América amid criticism») Vanessa Carvalho/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa The United States is set to host the Copa América for a second consecutive edition in 2028, drawing criticism that commercial interests are taking precedence over South American football tradition. South American governing body CONMEBOL and CONCACAF, which oversees football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, confirmed the decision on Tuesday. The US also hosted the 2024 Copa América and the 2025 Club World Cup, as well as most matches at this year's men's World Cup. The Los Angeles Olympics begin just days after the 2028 Copa América ends, while the US is also among the hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup. Ecuador had also expressed interest in staging the tournament for the first time since 1993. The decision drew criticism in South American media and on social media, with Chilean newspaper La Tercera suggesting the competition no longer belonged to South America. US outlet The Athletic also questioned the focus on revenue, arguing that the 110-year-old tournament risked losing cultural significance that money could not replace. First held in 1916, the Copa América is the oldest surviving continental football tournament for national teams. It was staged outside South America for the first time in 2016, also in the US. The 2028 edition is due to take place from June 9 to July 9, featuring all 10 CONMEBOL members and six CONCACAF teams.

Get to Know Evansville: An Improved Team From the MVC With a Cool Mascot The Purple Aces. It’s always fun going against a school with a unique mascot. Evansville coined the name after a local sports journalist said, “They played like Aces.” They were formerly the Evansville Pioneers until they made the change in the 1920s. The 20th century was extremely successful for the mid-major from Indiana. Evansville won five Division II national championships from 1959 to 1971 under the leadership of Arad McCutchan, who was the first coach inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, before jumping to Division I in 1977. The Purple Aces have since made five NCAA Tournament appearances, reaching as far as the second round in 1989, but haven’t been back on the national stage since 1999. Under fifth-year head coach David Ragland, Evansville has never finished higher than eighth in the Missouri Valley Conference. The Purple Aces are coming off a 7-25 season (3-17 MVC). They should improve upon that performance with more continuity than other mid-majors that Mizzou has seen this season. Evansville is already out to a 3-3 record this season, including a 79-65 win over a Le Moyne team that the Tigers beat 91-64. The solid start can be largely credited to the rise of sophomore guard Bryce Quinet, who’s averaging 18.3 points, eight assists and 1.3 steals per game. He’s one of three key returners that Ragland got back this season to lay a foundation. James Dyson-Merwe is also in his sophomore season, contributing 7.3 points and 4.7 rebounds per game off the bench. item.title: 49ers safety gets last laugh against Seattle ahead of crucial NFC West showdown
item.description: Malik Mustapha receives a fine for a hit on JSN. 49ers safety Malik Mustapha is saving money. On Tuesday, NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed that Mustapha, who appealed his fine from the league, won his case for a hit he made against Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Malik Mustapha celebrating in an NFL game against the Vikings last Sunday. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mustapha’s appeal was overseen by former Packers wide receiver Jordy Nelson, who served as the hearing officer, and the 49ers player will save $6,998. Mustapha was running toward Smith-Njigba on a pass play. Once the ball hit Smith-Njigba’s hands, the two collided — resulting in the ball popping out of the reigning Offensive Player of the Year’s hands for an incompletion. Upon appeal, the NFL rescinded the $6,998 fine it assessed to 49ers S Malik Mustapha for this hit earlier in the season on Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Jordy Nelson was the hearing officer. The 49ers and Seahawks play again Sunday. pic.twitter.com/S0IU2KwFiw — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 Mustapha rose to his feet quickly after the play, while Smith-Njigba rolled over on his stomach area and momentarily remained on the ground. While Mustapha hopes to put the play behind him, the Seahawks likely haven’t forgotten about it ahead of Sunday’s game. Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba running with the ball during an NFL game. Getty Images When the teams met in Seattle earlier this season, the 49ers put together a 32-29 statement victory to not only forget about last season’s 41-6 playoff loss to the Seahawks but also propel them to the top of the NFC West. Quarterback Brock Purdy was 19-of-29 passing for 189 yards with two touchdowns and one interception that put him in the MVP conversation. Purdy executed a 12-play drive in the first half and completed 6 of 7 passes — four of which went to Mike Evans for 75 yards. 49ers defense celebrating in an NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys. AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez Purdy’s heroics from the first half carried into the second. The Niners executed 13 plays on a drive that started in the third and carried into the fourth quarter. San Francisco capped it with a 7-yard touchdown reception to Brandin Cooks and followed it with a two-point conversion to Evans. Seattle tied the game at 29 with 6:59 left, but San Francisco answered with a field goal. The 49ers’ defense held the Seahawks to only five plays before it forced a turnover on downs, and San Francisco ran out the clock. The Niners (9-1) not only have a chance to solidify themselves as the NFC West’s best team but also have an opportunity to move further ahead in the NFC standings. Seattle (6-4), the defending Super Bowl champion, is hoping a victory would keep it in the wild-card race.

item.title: ‘Is Jim Harbaugh Okay?’ ‘Ooof’ — NFL Podcaster Sounds Alarm After Chargers HC Asks Staff for Help With Basic Question in Press Conference
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh on the sidelines against the New York Jets during the second half at SoFi Stadium. © Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Chargers are in one of the worst starts in franchise history, sitting at 1-9 through 10 games. Few saw this coming, as the Chargers were expected to be playoff contenders at the start of the season. However, things could not have gone worse for LA this season. They have been terrible on both sides of the ball, and it is hard not to blame the coaching staff for their downfall. Head coach Jim Harbaugh was hired in 2024 to change the franchise’s fortunes. Despite back-to-back 11-win seasons to begin his tenure, this season could force the Chargers to make a change. Something seems off with Harbaugh this season, and his recent press conference made that clear. Jim Harbaugh Confused By Simple Question on Chargers’ Press Conference During his midweek press conference, Harbaugh was asked about the “green dot” on defense and the player wearing it. The green dot identifies the defensive player equipped with a helmet radio receiver who gets the play call from the coaching staff and relays it to his teammates. Despite being the head coach, he did not know which player was making the calls. NFL podcaster Tony Farmer made some comments on the video, saying, “Oooof. Have you ever seen a coach unaware of who is calling plays on his defense? Is Jim Harbaugh okay?” It is not a great look for Harbaugh, and his confusion raises the question of whether he is fully bought into coaching this team. The Chargers front office will face a tough decision after the season, especially because Harbaugh was brought in to change the Chargers’ culture. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Harbaugh has been a successful head coach everywhere he has been. He took the San Francisco 49ers to the Super Bowl back in 2012 before winning a National Championship at Michigan in 2023. The 1-9 start is among the worst stretches of Harbaugh’s coaching career, although he has endured losing seasons before, including at Stanford and during Michigan’s shortened 2020 season. The Chargers have had starting quarterback Justin Herbert all season. This makes this season more of an indictment of Harbaugh. Usually, when we see terrible teams, they either lack a franchise quarterback or that quarterback gets injured. Neither applies to the 2026 Chargers. The Chargers have the second-worst Offense Impact Score in the NFL at 65.0. That is an indictment of Harbaugh, who is an offensive coach, as they have been abysmal at putting points on the board. Herbert has taken a step back this season, and Harbaugh, along with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, deserve blame for that, believe fans and analysts. item.title: 'I don't even know how the playoffs work': Georgia's Joseph Jonah-Ajonye just like everyone else with CFP rankings
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect College football players: they’re just like us! Each Tuesday, we’re greeted with a new round of seeding for the upcoming College Football Playoff. We’re told these rankings matter, but with the logic and reasoning shifting week to week, it’s hard to see why we’re supposed to care . This year’s logic pretzel around why Alabama has been ahead of Tennessee, even though the Volunteers beat them, is the latest in the long series of confusing decisions . Heck, last year we found out the committee will just reverse its thinking at the last moment if it chooses to. The whole exercise can leave you wondering if you even understand how the College Football Playoff works. And you wouldn’t be alone. Before Georgia’s regular-season finale against Georgia Tech this weekend, DL Joseph Jonah-Ajonye was asked if he or his teammates watch the weekly College Football Playoff Rankings show and think about how it might impact who they play in the first round. To his credit, Jonah-Ajonye has absolutely no idea what you’re talking about. I’m not gonna lie to you, I don’t [watch the rankings show]. If I’m gonna be completely honest, I don’t even know how the playoffs work for real,” Jonah-Ajonye said . “You just line up and play; that’s all I do for real.” Quote of the day comes from UGA DL Joseph Jonah-Ajonye on the CFP rankings. “If I’m gonna be honest, I don’t even know how the playoffs work. You just line up and play, that’s all I do for real.” https://t.co/yC5hXGJpMS — Connor Riley (@Kconnorriley) November 24, 2026 To be fair, we can only imagine the hell he’d have to pay Georgia coach Kirby Smart if he said he cared about what the CFP rankings said in November. But regardless, it goes to show just how meaningless and unnecessarily confusing the whole exercise is. Whatever happens, you better believe the Bulldogs will be up there when the final CFP selections happen. At 10-1, they’ve already clinched a spot in the SEC Championship Game. If they keep doing what they’ve been doing most of the season, Jonah-Ajonye won’t have to figure anything out because the CFP committee will for them. item.title: Reaction: “We broke them down with our intensity”
item.description: Reaction: “We broke them down with our intensity” (in the mixed zone): “For me, this game is a real statement. When you go 1-0 down against the English champions, you know what sort of opposition you’re facing. After all, Arsenal are currently top of the English league too. To come back like that, make it an even contest in the first half and then really show the courage to push for an equaliser in the second, perhaps even want a little more – that was impressive. At the same time, we defended our goal together. I think the players really showed they were a team today and stood up for one another. If someone made a mistake, someone else stepped in. Everyone kept throwing themselves in front of shots and into challenges today, doing everything they could to defend our goal. So a huge compliment to the team. Coming away from here with a point is a great achievement.” Ole Book (in the mixed zone): “We’re really happy with the point and with our performance in the second half. It might not have been our best game, but it was still a pretty good one. There are few tougher challenges than playing away at Arsenal – and then going behind. To stand up to them like that and grow stronger shows that the lads believe in themselves and that we believe in what we’re building together. Every point is a huge help in our bid to progress.” Niko Kovac (at the press conference): “It’s a big point for us. A big moment for all of us – for the team and for the fans, who turned out in such numbers today. Of course, we’re happy to take the point in the end. We’re here in London, so naturally there will be moments you have to weather. I think the team showed a really good side of themselves today. You certainly can’t accuse them of hiding or not giving everything. We fought as a team, kept responding and showed that we can hold our own against strong opposition too.” Nico Schlotterneck (on Prime): “We were extremely poor in the first 15 minutes, when we showed very little courage and were lucky not to go 2-0 down. We were very sleepy and barely got out of our own half. The lads did really well in the second half. We broke them down with our intensity. We went man-to-man throughout the second half and won our individual battles. Joane Gadou had an incredible game and produced a moment of individual brilliance to create a great goal together with Maxi Beier. Arsenal put us under a bit of pressure again in the last 15 minutes. The lads really fought for this point. As captain, I’m very pleased.” Jobe Bellingham (in the mixed zone): “The team are pretty proud. Coming away with a point in the end is probably fair and feels good. We came to a difficult place and still got a positive result. Our performance got better as the game went on. item.title: Zamfara gov’t suspends campaign after road crash
item.description: The Zamfara government has suspended its scheduled campaign activities in Maru Local Government Area following a road accident that killed 15 APC supporters. The victims died along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route while travelling to Talata Mafara for the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) confirmed that 15 people died, while 27 others sustained injuries in the crash. The accident occurred at about 12.30 p.m. on Monday near Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route. The government announced the suspension in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Dantawasa, on Monday in Gusau. Dantawasa said the accident involved APC members travelling from Gummi Local Government Area. “The government expresses its deep sorrow over the unfortunate incident and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said. He also extended condolences to the Gummi Emirate and the APC family in Zamfara over the loss. The commissioner said the government sympathised with the injured and prayed for their speedy recovery. “In this moment of grief, the Zamfara State Government stands in solidarity with the affected families and all those mourning the loss of their loved ones,” he said. He urged residents to remain calm and offer prayers for the deceased and injured. “May Almighty Allah forgive the souls of the departed, grant them Aljannatul Firdaus, and give their families the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” Dantawasa said. The post Zamfara gov’t suspends campaign after road crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebonyi govt approves 933.777 hectares for smart city, dredging of 3.3km Ebonyi River against flooding
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has approved the establishment of a 933.777-hectare of new city called FON Smart City in Abakaliki, alongside the dredging of 3,305.61 metres of the Ebonyi River as part of measures to expand the state capital and mitigate potential flooding. The approvals were granted by the State Executive Council (EXCO), presided over by Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, during its meeting. The Commissioner for Information and State Orientation, Chief Ikeuwa Omebeh ehike briefing journalists on the outcome of the Exco meeting, said the proposed smart city would be developed on an additional 933.777 hectares of land acquired from the former Army land within Abakaliki capital. Omebeh explained that the council had approved the designation of the newly acquired territory and its entire development layout as FON Smart City, Abakaliki. He said the initiative was part of the Nwifuru administration’s strategic urban development agenda aimed at expanding the territorial boundaries of the state capital, attracting private-sector investments and stimulating economic activities. According to him, the proposed smart city has been designed with clearly defined land-use zones to accommodate the state’s growing residential, commercial, institutional and developmental requirements. He listed the components of the master plan to include residential neighbourhoods, institutional zones, commercial districts, a Central Business District, green verges, agricultural and farming zones, community resettlement areas and special provision areas. The commissioner said the carefully structured development framework was intended to create a modern urban environment capable of accommodating future population growth while improving the infrastructural capacity, aesthetics and economic outlook of Abakaliki. He added that the project would open up new investment opportunities, expand economic activities and strengthen Ebonyi State’s position as an emerging investment destination in the South-East. Also, the State Executive Council approved the dredging of approximately 3,305.61 metres (3.3 kilometres) of the Ebonyi River to address potential flooding threats within sections of the proposed smart city. Omebeh said the decision followed the identification of flood-prone areas within the proposed development corridor, necessitating proactive environmental intervention to safeguard the planned urban infrastructure. He explained that the dredging exercise would improve water flow, reduce flooding risks and provide the necessary environmental protection for the sustainable development of the new city. The commissioner stressed that the government’s decision to incorporate flood-control measures into the smart city project underscored its commitment to sustainable urban planning and the protection of public infrastructure against environmental hazards. item.title: Surgeons offer free knee replacements as orthopaedic association begins AGM
item.description: … Over 100 patients receive free treatment in Abuja outreach By Ruth Onyekachi No fewer than 100 people living with disabling bone and joint conditions received free medical attention on Monday as Nigerian orthopaedic surgeons began a three-day surgical outreach in Abuja, offering procedures, including costly knee replacements, to patients who cannot afford them. The outreach, organised by the Nigerian Orthopaedic Association (NOA) as part of activities marking its 49th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Scientific Conference, will run until Wednesday across five hospitals in the Federal Capital Territory. The participating facilities are Wuse District Hospital, Garki Hospital, Federal Medical Centre, Abuja, Cedarcrest Hospital and Alliance Hospital, where orthopaedic surgeons drawn from across the country are providing consultations, surgeries and post-operative care at no cost to beneficiaries. For many of the patients, the intervention represents an opportunity to access procedures that would ordinarily cost millions of naira, particularly knee replacement surgeries that remain beyond the reach of low-income Nigerians. Vice President of the association, Dr Christian Madubueze, who represented its President, Dr E.A. Orimolade, said the outreach was part of NOA’s commitment to making specialised orthopaedic care accessible to underserved Nigerians. “This is not the first time we have done an outreach with the FCT — we did one during our 2023 AGM that was hosted here, and we were very happy, we were well treated, and we were able to serve patients,” he said. He disclosed that the association would undertake a significant number of knee replacement operations free of charge. “We are doing a significant number of knee replacement surgeries which normally would have cost these patients millions of naira, but we as an association are going to do them here,” he explained. Madubueze said the choice of established hospitals was deliberate because complex procedures such as joint replacement require standard operating theatres and specialised facilities. “It is actually not possible for us to be doing this in the villages unless we are going to set up a makeshift hospital there, which will dramatically increase the cost,” he said, adding that “Wuse District Hospital is very important to us.” The FCT administration also welcomed the initiative, describing it as an important intervention for residents who struggle to access specialised medical services. Director of Clinical Services, Dr Osayande Osagie, who represented the Mandate Secretary for Health Services and Environment, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, said the administration appreciated the association for bringing the services closer to the people. “Orthopaedic surgery or consultations are not things that are cheap to find, especially in a town like Abuja,” Osagie said. “This corporate social responsibility that you brought to the people of Abuja, we really appreciate it, and on their behalf I want to say a big

item.title: Nigerian children: Millions still face barriers to education, protection
item.description: …Demand free education, stronger safeguards, greater voice in decisions By Chioma Obinna For millions of Nigerian children, the promise of a safe childhood, quality education and a future shaped by their dreams remains a daily struggle. From access to basic education and healthcare to protection from abuse and poverty, the gap between children’s rights and their lived realities continues to raise concerns about the country’s commitment to its youngest population. The challenge came into focus on Friday as the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government marked the 2026 World Children’s Day, calling for stronger protection of children’s rights and concrete government action to secure their future. At the celebration, held at the UNICEF Lagos Office under the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future,” children demanded free education, greater protection and a stronger voice in decisions affecting their lives. UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, warned that children’s rights were increasingly under threat globally, stressing that governments and other stakeholders must do more to guarantee access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. She noted that recognising children’s rights was not enough if families and communities lacked the resources to make those rights meaningful. Lafoucriere explained that social protection programmes were essential to helping vulnerable children access basic services, particularly education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said. She stressed that UNICEF was working with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to every child, particularly those from vulnerable backgrounds. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” she declared, urging society to recognise that investment in children could not be postponed. Children want more than promises Beyond the concerns raised by development partners and government officials, the celebration provided an opportunity for children to articulate their expectations of those responsible for protecting their rights. The Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Rt. Hon. Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their welfare, insisting that their experiences and opinions must count when policies concerning them are formulated. He said children were often better positioned to explain the challenges they faced, particularly cases of abuse and other threats to their safety. Anjola also urged the government to increase investment in education and create opportunities for children who were out of school. “Education is the weapon that can instigate war,” he said, calling for

item.title: ESUT remains committed to quality academic standards, VC tells NUC accreditation teams
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—The Vice-Chancellor of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, on Tuesday , reaffirmed the university’s commitment to sustaining high academic standards, strengthening quality assurance and improving service delivery. Professor Okolie gave the assurance when accreditation teams from the National Universities Commission (NUC), responsible for Civil Engineering and Mechanical and Production Engineering programmes, visited the university to assess the programmes. He commended the NUC for its efforts in upholding academic standards in Nigeria’s tertiary education system, noting that ESUT had prioritised practical training for staff and students to equip them with the skills needed to address challenges within their immediate environment and the country at large. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that the university had signed a partnership agreement with a Qatar-based Information and Communication Technology (ICT) firm, Vertex Labs, to establish a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (AI). He added that representatives of the company were expected to arrive soon to expand the scope of the partnership to include the fabrication of computer accessories. According to him, the initiative builds on the selection of ESUT by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) as a South-East Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Cybersecurity and other related fields. Professor Okolie also disclosed that the university management had inaugurated an ICT Innovation Hub to provide staff and students with practical training and professional certification programmes that would enhance their employability and economic independence after graduation. He emphasised the importance of engineering in driving the university’s innovation agenda, adding that the institution makes adequate preparations for accreditation exercises by setting aside special funds ahead of time. The Vice-Chancellor further acknowledged TETFund’s contributions towards the procurement of equipment required for accreditation exercises and assured the visiting teams of the full support and cooperation of the university management. Speaking at the ESUT Council Chamber, the leader of the Civil Engineering accreditation team, Professor Mohammed Saidu, said the exercise was not intended to witch-hunt the university but to objectively assess its compliance with established academic standards. He assured the university that the teams would discharge their responsibilities with professionalism, objectivity and due diligence. The accreditation team for Mechanical and Production Engineering was led by Professor Aje Tokan of the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi State. item.title: Zero-dose children: Lagos, Kano charged to sustain immunisation gains
item.description: …As GSK-supported Save The Children BOOST project approaches 2027 close-out By Sola Ogundipe Lagos and Kano States have been urged to take full ownership of the Better Opportunities for Optimal Services and Targeted Immunisation for Zero-Dose and Under-Immunised Children (BOOST) programme towards making adequate budgetary provisions to sustain its gains ahead of the project’s expected close-out in 2027. The call came amid continuing efforts to bridge Nigeria’s zero-dose and under-immunisation gaps, with stakeholders warning that local ownership, sustainable financing and stronger primary healthcare delivery will be critical to ensuring that children are not left unprotected when donor-supported interventions end. BOOST is a four-year initiative funded by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and implemented by Save the Children International (SCI) in Lagos and Kano States. It seeks to reduce the number of children who have never received routine vaccines or have missed important doses in their immunisation schedules. The programme is built around the principle that no child should be left unprotected against vaccine-preventable diseases because of where they live, their family’s economic circumstances or weaknesses in the healthcare system. Stakeholders who made the call in Abuja during the Lessons Learning and Transition Planning Workshop organised by SCI with support from GSK, urged government officials and civil society organisations from both states to review the project’s sustainability prospects, share best practices and develop strategies for transferring successful interventions to government-led interventions. Participants said sustaining improvements in immunisation coverage and reducing the number of zero-dose and under-immunised children would depend on state governments adopting successful project innovations, strengthening partnerships with civil society organisations and maintaining community engagement beyond the programme’s lifespan. The Policy and Advocacy Coordinator of the GSK-supported BOOST Project in Lagos State, Dr Itunu Dave-Agboola, said the programme had recorded significant improvements in immunisation coverage and acceptance across its intervention local government areas. “I would say the project has been successful because, looking at data coming in from the intervention LGAs, there’s a significant improvement in immunisation coverage and acceptance. We have enjoyed effective collaboration from the governments of both states, both at the level of the Ministry of Health and Primary Health Care Board. They have been very supportive and collaborative. We supported them to implement a lot of their activities. “The collaboration is a strong one such that we see sustainability even beyond the life of the BOOST project, because that is the most important thing, sustainability, so that the gains of this project will not be lost in transit,” she said. item.title: Discos’ Band A of sorrow
item.description: By SUNNY IKHIOYA The time for another round of elections is drawing close. The people seem to be unaware of where to hold the government responsible. Politicians are only concerned about personal insults and vain things. But in recent times, they have upped the tempo to begin to talk about petroleum subsidy and palliatives for the common man. One thing that the people have not been sensitive about is the fraudulent manner in which the electricity distribution companies are taking advantage of the government’s inability to monitor their activities properly. The NERC, the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission, is there, invisible to consumers. We have also been informed that some states have established their own regulatory commissions, like Lagos, Enugu and others. They, too, do not seem to be making their presence felt. Just like petrol, electricity is also at the centre of a people’s development. A country that cannot independently generate its own electricity is as good as staying dead at the bottom. Manufacturers cannot produce, skilled and small businesses will not grow, and the people will remain unhappy. Presently, the high-handedness of the electricity distribution companies is a principal cause of the downward drop in our poverty ratings. The middle class has been completely wiped out, businesses are dying, and no one seems to care. You know why our situation is so despicable: the state of Iran has been at war with the US and Israel for close to a year now, with critical infrastructure badly destroyed. In the midst of all these disruptions, it is still able to supply vital electricity to its people and businesses. The same thing is happening to Ukraine against Russia. Without light, the people are finished. It is a basic principle and also has some spiritual undertone. When you have light, you prevail over challenges and adversaries. That is why our situation is so pathetic. And so they came up with the structuring of the billing system, arguing that with a cost-reflective—no subsidy—tariff system in place, the power companies could be motivated to produce satisfactory power supply to the people and businesses. They embarked on classifying consumers into Classes A–D categories. Although this did not go well with the people, because it clearly was discriminatory and assumed to favour only the wealthy class, it has all turned out to be a scam on the consumers in that category. The Discos have used the monopoly they possess to fleece innocent consumers and businesses of their hard-earned income, with many of them finding it difficult to cope. Yet, on a monthly basis, the bills will arrive. In announcing the cost-reflective tariffs, the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission emphasised that Band A customers will enjoy a minimum of 20 hours of uninterrupted power supply in a day. They went further to say that, if the Discos are unable to meet up with the terms and conditions of the Band A category, the tariffs must be adjusted downwar

item.title: 2027: Shunning ethnicity and religion
item.description: As Nigerians prepare for next year’s general elections, they must move beyond the unhealthy politics of ethnicity and religion in the campaigns and choice of leaders. While diversity and equitable representation deserve recognition, they must not take precedence over competence, accountability and proven track records of service delivery. Nigeria cannot build a united democracy on religious intolerance, ethnic suspicion and political exclusion. The country’s numerous ethnic nationalities, languages, cultures and religious traditions should be sources of strength. Sadly, politicians and influential interest groups increasingly manipulate these identities to deepen divisions, promote intolerance and weaken national unity. The emerging political atmosphere is reminiscent of the 2023 general elections, when ethnic and religious considerations dominated campaigns and public discourse. The European Union Election Observation Mission (EU-EOM), in its final report, expressed concern over divisive language and the mobilisation of ethnic and religious sentiments during the elections. It is particularly disturbing that candidates are increasingly judged not by their competence, records and policy proposals but by their faith, language or geographical origin. Political differences or disagreements are sinisterly framed as grievances against entire ethnic or religious communities. Such tendencies undermine democratic competition and threaten peaceful coexistence. The Constitution (1999, as amended) provides clear safeguards against this divisive politics. Section 10 prohibits the adoption of any religion as a state religion, while Section 15 promotes national integration and prohibits discrimination based on place of origin, religion, ethnic or linguistic association. Section 42 further guarantees protection against discrimination on these grounds. These provisions must translate into political practice. No Nigerian should be denied the opportunity to aspire to public office because of religious belief or ethnic origin. Equally, political appointments and access to public opportunities must be guided by fairness, merit and competence rather than narrow identity considerations. Religious leaders must also recognise their responsibility to promote peace, tolerance and mutual respect. Pulpits and religious platforms should never become instruments for spreading political hatred or hostility against people of other faiths. Traditional rulers, community leaders and ethnic associations must similarly resist manipulation by partisan interests. Cultural pride should never become an excuse for intolerance. Politicians who exploit religious and ethnic sentiments for electoral advantage must understand that the divisions they create often outlive their political ambitions. The consequences can undermine national cohesion long after elections have ended. item.title: Taxation or imposition: The state, economy and citizenship in Nigeria (2), by Usman Sarki
item.description: “We cannot demand twenty-first-century compliance with twentieth-century communication .” — Mohammed Idris Bultu The first part of this article examined taxation as a relationship between the state and the citizen and ended with a fundamental question: what does the state owe the citizen after collecting his money? Two thoughtful responses to that article have since helped to sharpen the inquiry considerably. Barrister Muhammad Betara, an Abuja-based lawyer, approached the subject mainly from the standpoint of law and public administration, while Mohammed Idris Bultu, a Tax Controller with the Nigeria Revenue Service in Kano, responded from the practical experience of a tax administrator who encounters taxpayers, assessments, compliance and collection in the field. Taken together, their observations provide an important bridge between theory, law and administrative practice. Barrister Betara’s central point is that Nigeria is not without a legal framework for taxation. On the contrary, the Constitution and the recent tax reforms impose clear duties upon citizens and create elaborate machinery for assessment, collection and administration. According to him, Section 24(f) of the 1999 Constitution places upon every citizen the duty to declare his income honestly and pay his tax promptly. That obligation is direct and enforceable. At the same time, the Constitution declares that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government and places upon the state broad responsibilities relating to economic welfare, justice and social order. Betara’s important observation is that an imbalance exists between these two sides of the constitutional bargain. The citizen’s obligation to pay tax is concrete and enforceable, while many of the wider welfare obligations of government cannot be enforced by the citizen in quite the same manner. This immediately raises the problem of reciprocity. If the state possesses machinery to compel compliance from the citizen, what equivalent machinery exists which enables the citizen to compel transparency, accountability and adequate service delivery from the state? This lies very close to the heart of the distinction between taxation and imposition. The recent tax reforms have sought to strengthen and modernise the administrative capacity of government. They aim to harmonise tax administration, rationalise procedures, improve taxpayer identification, expand the tax base and provide mechanisms for objection and appeal. Barrister Betara therefore makes the important point that the Nigerian problem is not simply the absence of laws. The problem is that the machinery of collection often appears stronger, more visible and more immediate than the machinery of public accountability. Tax Officer Mohammed Bultu’s practical observations reinforce this point from another direction. His first proposition is simple but profound: legitimacy makes collection possible.
