item.title: Saving Enyimba FC from relegation, by Ochereome Nnanna
item.description: This article is not about football per se. It is about Enyimba International Football Club of Aba, Abia State. Before the coming of our phenomenal and algorithmic Governor, Dr Alex C. Otti, to the saddle, Enyimba FC was about the only thing that made us Abians proud of our state. We were like the eagle chained by bad governance for so long that we forgot to fly. Enyimba is the most prestigious and dominant force in Nigerian football. Three football clubs have historically personified the irrepressible, resilient, successful and enterprising spirit for which the Igbo nation is famous all over the world. The Enugu Rangers International served notice that though we lost the Biafra War, we were not a defeated people. However, though the Rangers dominated Nigerian football and the Green Eagles in the 1970s, their Ibadan rivals, IICC Shooting Stars, beat them to the first achievement of winning the African Winners Cup in 1976. The following year, Rangers achieved the same feat, but IICC fans retain the bragging rights of being there first. Later on, the Spartans FC of Owerri, which was formed around the same time as Enyimba in 1976, became Iwuanyanwu Nationale and dominated the so-called “professional” era. The Owerri club was renamed Heartland FC, a name it wore until it was relegated for the fourth time to the Nigeria National League (NNL) on 25th May 2025 under the hand of Governor Hope Uzodimma. Its first relegation took place in 2016. Imo has seemingly ceased to be a notable footballing state despite an abundance of talents. Enyimba FC of Aba is the real “agba baller” of Nigerian football. It is to Nigeria what Real Madrid is to Spain. It also compares only to Liverpool FC in England in terms of comprehensive domestic dominance and continental conquests. Enyimba remains the only Nigerian club to win the CAF Champions League – back-to-back in 2003 and 2004 – with two African Super Cups. This is apart from dominating in the local league and sharing top prizes in the FA Cup series. If there is any one lasting legacy for which Senator Orji Uzor Kalu will be forever remembered, it is the Enyimba CAF Champions League achievements, which happened under his watch as Governor of Abia State. If you check how our mighty Enyimba FC is doing in the 14th week of the current NPFL season, you will be shocked to see it slumbering in the 18th position – topping the relegation zone! That was how Heartland started before it became a regular customer in the second-class NNL. God forbid that Enyimba will suffer this fate. It will be so abominable, a taboo! Experience has shown that once a mighty club tastes relegation, it always goes back for more. Enyimba must NEVER be relegated! It must return to its pride of place – at the top currently occupied by its elder brother, Rangers. In truth, Enyimba has been suffering since 2015 when Dr Okezie Ikpeazu took over as governor. item.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
item.description: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate. Read full article Comments

item.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
item.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. Those missions were also launched aboard Falcon 9 rockets, also with undisclosed payloads.

item.title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
item.description: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide. Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote. The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Tambuwal commends Gov Ododo for granting ADC access to Buhari Square
item.description: Former Sokoto State Governor and African Democratic Congress chieftain, Aminu Tambuwal, has commended Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, for allowing the ADC to hold its rally at Muhammadu Buhari Square in the state. Tambuwal described the gesture as an act of statesmanship, saying political differences should not prevent leaders from respecting democratic rights and promoting peaceful coexistence. In a post on X on Tuesday, he thanked Ododo for granting the opposition party access to the venue, noting that such actions strengthened democracy and encouraged political tolerance. “I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Governor of Kogi State, His Excellency, for his commendable show of statesmanship in granting the African Democratic Congress (ADC) the use of Muhammadu Buhari Square for its rally in Kogi State,” he said. Tambuwal said the governor’s action demonstrated that disagreements over political affiliations should not undermine the right of citizens and parties to participate in the democratic process. He said democracy was strengthened when political leaders respected the constitutional rights of others to assemble, associate and express their views regardless of party differences. The former governor also praised Kogi residents for their conduct during the rally, commending them for maintaining peace and order throughout the event. Tambuwal urged political leaders to promote tolerance and avoid treating political opponents as adversaries, stressing that disagreements should be settled through the exchange of ideas. “Democracy is not a contest of enemies but a contest of ideas, and that our political differences must never overshadow our shared commitment to the peace, unity and progress of our country,” he said. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
item.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. But credibility requires more than reducing the headline figure. Government should publish exactly which programmes are being removed, reduced, de

item.title: I have an incurable form of cancer - Farooq Oreagba opens up
item.description: The Managing Director of NG Clearing Limited, Farooq Oreagba, has disclosed that he is living with an incurable form of cancer, saying his treatment is progressing well and he hopes to return to remission next year. The 60-year-old investment banker said he was diagnosed on February 4 following a medical screening but had continued working and maintaining his lifestyle despite the condition. In an interview with TheCable Lifestyle on Monday, Oreagba said he had learnt to manage the illness and remained optimistic about his recovery. “I have an incurable form of cancer. It comes, I treat, and it goes. I was diagnosed in February, after which I rode at Ojude Oba, celebrated my 60th and continued as if nothing was wrong,” he said. Oreagba said he was responding well to treatment and expected to return to remission around March or April 2027. “I am very fine, working as usual and doing what I always do. My treatment is going well, and I expect to be back in remission by March/April next year,” he added. Popularly known as the ‘King of Steeze’, Oreagba became an internet sensation in 2024 after his stylish appearance and horseback display at the Ojude Oba Festival in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State, attracted widespread attention. However, his battle with cancer dates back to 2014, when he was diagnosed with bone marrow and skin cancer. He underwent a transplant in August of that year and has since continued managing the condition, receiving treatment in Johannesburg, South Africa. Oreagba urged Nigerians to prioritise routine medical examinations, saying his condition was detected early during a screening exercise. He said he undergoes medical checks every three months, adding that people should not wait until they experience symptoms before seeking medical attention. “Early detection saves lives, and I recommend regular checks. I do mine every three months, but even every six months would suffice,” he said. He added, “It is important to know that a cancer diagnosis is not a death sentence. I am making great progress.” The post I have an incurable form of cancer - Farooq Oreagba opens up appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal: Earlier hearing date still being pursued — Lawyer
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The legal team of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, says efforts are still being considered to secure an earlier hearing date for his appeal against conviction, insisting that the January 25, 2027 date is not sacrosanct. Kanu’s Special Counsel, Aloy Ejimakor, disclosed this in a press release on Tuesday, clarifying that the legal team had contemplated moving the appeal forward almost two months ago when the January 25 date was initially communicated to Kanu and his lawyers. Ejimakor said the decision to seek an earlier hearing had remained unchanged, dismissing any impression that the scheduled date was a settled matter. He explained that the Rules of Court allow an appellant to formally apply for an abridgment of time, a procedural mechanism through which a court can be asked to fast-track an appeal and hear it earlier than originally scheduled. According to him, the option remains under active consideration in view of the critical issues involved in the appeal and the urgency attached to it. “Nothing is yet set in stone,” Ejimakor declared, assuring that legal avenues for expediting the hearing remained available and were being carefully weighed to prevent justice from being delayed. The clarification comes amid expectations surrounding Kanu’s appeal, with his legal team signalling its intention to explore available judicial procedures to bring forward the hearing date. Ejimakor, who signed the statement on behalf of Kanu, said the pursuit of an earlier date had been on the table since the original January 25, 2027, date was made known to the defendant and his lawyers. The legal team, however, did not disclose whether an application for abridgment of time had already been formally filed or when such an application might be made. Kanu was sentenced to life imprisonment since November, 2025, and his efforts to appeal the judgment have suffered unnecessary setbacks for one year. The post Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal: Earlier hearing date still being pursued — Lawyer appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NASA+ Content Coming to Big Screen at Greenbelt, Maryland Cinema
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA announced Monday that NASA+ content has found its first theatrical home at The Greenbelt Cinema in Greenbelt, Maryland, expanding the agency’s reach across major viewing platforms and bringing space even closer to home. “The National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 calls us to share our story of space exploration with the broadest possible audience, and our partners help us accomplish that,” said Rebecca Sirmons, general manager of NASA+ at the agency’s Headquarters in Washington. “Artemis II captured the imagination of the Artemis generation, but we are just getting started. With Artemis III on the horizon and our sights set on building humanity’s first Moon Base, this is only the beginning of our story being told, and we’ll continue sharing transparent, engaging content every step of the way.” NASA and The Greenbelt Cinema will kick off their partnership with screenings of the NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Concept,” which follows NASA’s journey to investigate the science driving future exploration of Europa, Jupiter’s icy moon. Dates for screenings will be announced soon on NASA.gov. Future programming may include other NASA+ original content, in-person live streaming events of NASA’s Artemis missions, including the first crewed mission to the Moon under the Artemis program, additional Europa content, and more. NASA+ also will remain available for free, with no ads, through the NASA app and on the agency’s website . Earlier this year during its Ignition event, NASA outlined a bold path forward for the agency, including increasing the cadence of Artemis missions to the lunar surface, and building the first Moon Base , among other agency priorities. Partnerships like this one help NASA maximize engagement with communities around the world by making the agency’s missions and educational content available to viewers on their preferred devices and channels. For more information about NASA missions, visit: https://www.nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 24, 2026 Related Terms NASA+

item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act. item.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
item.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

item.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." (Image credit: Prime Video) Johnson admits that Louisa's pitch approval was just the opening round of a multitude of responsible decisions to be ruminated over as the production process advanced. "Once you agree that this is the story we’re telling, then it becomes a multi-year partnership in honoring all the artists and visionaries that came before as it relates to visual design and music," he notes. "Everything needs to be of the highest quality. Even though it's a TV show we feel it has theatrical level visual effec

item.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun torches Anthropic CEO over AI gatekeeping
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products. In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.” “Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed. “He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.” LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models. Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models. Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year. The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse. “Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read. Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post. Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models. In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own. LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory. item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

item.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
item.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

item.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
item.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
item.description: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Mission 25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 spacecraft is named in honor of NASA astronaut James “Jim” A. Lovell Jr. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Credit: NASA NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the Cygnus spacecraft’s approach and rendezvous. Watkins will be at the controls of the Canadarm2 robotic arm, ready to capture Cygnus as Delaney monitors the spacecraft’s arrival. Credit: NASA Science highlights In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes: Cardinal Muscle 2.0 Preflight image of the Biocell bioreactor system used to maintain engineered muscle tissue samples as part of the Advancing Therapeutic Treatment of Sarcopenia (Cardinal Muscle 2.0) investigation. Aboard the International Space Station, this investigation tests the effects of potential therapeutics on human muscle cell cultures. The research may help accelerate development of treatments for age-related muscle loss on Earth and support astronaut health during long-duration missions. Credit: Palo Alto Veteran’s Institute for Research Cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. item.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
item.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. (2026)) The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower

item.title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. From custodian to full-service bank Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025. The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks. The asset manager is the latest in a run of expansions. On Nov. 5, Anchorage Digital Swap Dealer LLC applied to th

item.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. Read full article Comments

item.title: Arm strongarms site that hosts ad-free documentation and it may disappear
item.description: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability. The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference , a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own. According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version. “The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans. That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture. Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else. As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form. “Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page. “I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen. Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation. "We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. item.title: An AI coding agent, a browser, and a Mac tool found a financial firm's access key in under 6 minutes
item.description: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes. It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine. “What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register . “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.” Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register , Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one. Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET. 'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking' OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work. “Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.” That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing. The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again. It used the same Chrome version, but said it was an Android Pixel 10 phone (it wasn’t) to see if the site would let a phone in (it didn’t). After failing to gain access through the front page, the

item.title: Microsoft refreshes Copilot app search for users without an AI subscription
item.description: Microsoft is updating search in its Microsoft 365 Copilot app for users without a Copilot license, with a toggle to restore the classic interface. Google, meanwhile, is giving AI searches more prominence on its homepage, where the familiar Search button is absent from a newly demonstrated layout. Microsoft's change is rolling out now and will hit Deferred Release by mid-January 2027. It will impact users with a Microsoft 365 license who do not have a Copilot license and "provides modern search controls to help users find, refine, and navigate search results more easily." It's enabled by default, which is a shame since administrators would likely prefer an opt-in rather than opt-out approach, and users can switch back to the "classic search experience" via a toggle on the search results page. Microsoft has not specified how long this toggle will remain available. Its separate Copilot Search experience had a fallback toggle scheduled for removal 60 days after general availability. "With the updated search experience, users can continue to find files using keywords, use modern search controls to refine and navigate results, and search supported connected third-party content when their organization has configured connected sources," Microsoft said. The results will still only display content to which users have permission. Microsoft advises administrators to brief users and help desks on the changed interface and the option to switch back. Microsoft's search tweaks arrive as the future of the Google Search button on Google's desktop homepage looks uncertain. In a post , Google VP of Product Robby Stein described a collapsible sidebar that lists users' recent AI conversations, pushing AI deeper into the search experience. Stein called it "a much simpler way to pick up where you left off," and said it would help customers "easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches." However, something else was obvious in Stein's post: the Google Search button was not present. Stein explained in August that Google had performed a "small test on desktop to help people find new things they can do with Search." Part of that test was the removal of the Google Search button. Users can still submit queries by pressing Enter. Stein said the test would have "no impact to how the core search works." The sidebar rollout doesn't itself confirm the Search button's permanent retirement. For now, its absence from Stein's demonstration is another sign of which features Google wants users to notice. ®

item.title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
item.description: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It wasn't until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche's upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that's usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance. item.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. Who found and exploited the flaw is still unknown, and law enforcement is investigating. The report calls AI

item.description: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government ( PDF ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China's lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA's, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there. item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity GRAND CAYMAN, Cayman Islands, Nov. 24, 2026. Stacks Labs today announced 1,050 BTC of capacity for Bond 4 of Bitcoin staking with Stacks, a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. The bond starts ~Dec. 5, and institutions can register at stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking. Bond 4 carries a 3% target annual yield, paid in BTC weekly over a six-month term. Each BTC staked is paired with STX worth 5% of its value, so filling Bond 4’s 1,050 BTC of capacity requires a corresponding STX commitment. Rewards come from Stacks miners, who commit BTC through Proof of Transfer (PoX), the consensus mechanism Stacks has run since January 2021. Every bond since the Genesis Bond launched in September has filled. 21shares returned for Bond 3, and Bullish (NYSE: BLSH) joined as the first top-10 public Bitcoin treasury company to stake BTC. “Opening more than 1,000 BTC of new capacity for institutions shows how strong the demand for Bitcoin yield has become,” said Muneeb Ali, CEO, Stacks Labs, and founder of Stacks. Institutions can stake from qualified custody, including BitGo. During the bootstrap phase, self-custodial Bitcoin staking is whitelisted. Holders who are not on the whitelist can take part through pooled Bitcoin staking at stacks.co/bitcoin-staking . About Stacks Stacks is a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. With Bitcoin staking, holders stake BTC with STX, and their BTC stays on the Bitcoin L1 under their own custody. Stacks has distributed over 4,200 BTC in rewards to participants since 2021. Learn more at stacks.co . item.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
item.description: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments
